title: Freedom Yield Metal — Identity History Leaf v1 (per-line)
description: Formal contract for EACH LINE of /api/identity-history.jsonl. The file is JSONL (line-delimited JSON): each line is one JSON object conforming to this schema and represents one operator-identity ed25519 key entry. Sorted by key_seq ascending (= 1, 2, 3, ...). Append-only within v1: a new key rotation appends a new line; an existing line is rewritten only when its revoked / revoked_at / revocation_reason transition from false to true, OR when superseded_by_key_seq is set on a previously authoritative key. The leaf source for identity_branch in the Merkle DAG; each line's SHA-256(raw_bytes_as_served) is one Merkle leaf. Companion spec: docs/MERKLE_DAG_SPEC.md §2.1. Schema stability: additive-only within v1; breaking changes go to /api/identity-history.schema.v2.json.
x-line-format: Each line of identity-history.jsonl validates against this schema independently. Use jq, ndjson tooling, or stream the file line-by-line.

key_seq.description: Monotone integer. key_seq=1 is the first operator-identity key. Used as the stable cross-reference target from cycle-history.jsonl.signed_by_key_seq.

operator_identity_pubkey_fingerprint.description: OpenSSH SHA-256:<base64>= fingerprint. Same value type as identity.json.operator_identity_pubkey_fingerprint at the time this key_seq was active. A verifier can compute the same fingerprint via 'ssh-keygen -l -f <pubkey>' and compare.

operator_identity_pubkey_url.description: URL where the public key bytes (OpenSSH 'ssh-ed25519 ...' line) were served at the time key_iat. For the current authoritative key this is /.well-known/operator-identity.pub. For superseded keys the operator MAY publish at /.well-known/operator-identity.v<key_seq>.pub to preserve verifiability of historical cycles; absence of a historical public key file is honest about its retirement and does not invalidate past cycle entries that reference this fingerprint.

key_iat.description: When this key became authoritative (ISO 8601 UTC).

key_exp.description: Operator-declared expiry (ISO 8601 UTC). NOT cryptographically enforced; consumers MAY treat as policy.

revoked.description: true iff this key is no longer authoritative AND has been explicitly revoked (not merely naturally superseded by a rotation). When true, revoked_at and revocation_reason MUST be non-null.

revocation_reason.description: Operator-supplied short reason; non-null iff revoked=true.

superseded_by_key_seq.description: Non-null on a key that has been rotated out by a higher key_seq for ANY reason (routine rotation OR revocation). For the currently authoritative key this is null. For a revoked key this points to the successor key_seq if one exists, else null.

comment.description: Optional operator-supplied human-readable note (e.g., 'initial production key', 'rotated for routine 12-month cadence'). Informational only; does not affect verification.
